'''Ikatsuno Mikoto''' (伊賀津臣命, {{ill|生没年不詳|ja|生没年不詳}}) was an ancient Japanese noble regarded as the founder of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ja|中臣連}}. In the *{{ill|Ōmi no Kuni Fudoki|ja|近江国風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omi no Kuni Fudoki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11638480}}* excerpts, he is referred to as '''Ikatsutomi''' or '''Ikatomi''', while one version of the *{{ill|Sonpi Bunmyaku|fa|سونپی بونمیاکو|fr|Sonpi bunmyaku|ja|尊卑分脈|zh|尊卑分脈|qid=Q1704738|lt=Sonpi Bunmyaku}}* refers to him as '''Ikatsuno Mikoto.'''

== Overview ==

Although he does not appear in the *{{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|ja|記紀|ko|기키|pl|Kiki (literatura japońska)|zh|記紀|qid=Q842308}}* and little is known about his accomplishments, Ikatsuno Mikoto features in the legend of the *{{ill|Hagoromo|en|Hagoromo|qid=Q1208551|lt=Hagoromo}}* (Celestial Robe of Feathers) recounted in the *{{ill|Ōmi no Kuni Fudoki|ja|近江国風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omi no Kuni Fudoki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11638480}}*. The text describes him as a resident of the mountains in the {{ill|Yogo District|ja|与胡郷}} in {{ill|Ōmi Province|en|Ōmi Province|qid=Q843882|lt=Ōmi Province}}. According to the story, Ikatsutomi spied on celestial maidens (*Amanohachime*, daughters of heaven) bathing with a swan in a nearby lake known as {{ill|Ikakoe|ja|伊香小江}} and fell in love at first sight. He sent a white dog to stealthily steal the celestial robe (*Hagoromo*) of the youngest maiden, thereby preventing her return to heaven. Ikatsutomi then married the celestial maiden and had four children: Omichito, {{ill|Nashitomi|ja|梨迹臣命|qid=Q108616765}}, Izerihime, and Nazerihime. The youngest celestial maiden eventually retrieved her robe and ascended back to heaven, leaving Ikatsutomi to live a lonely life.

Ikatsuno Mikoto is venerated as the enshrined deity of {{ill|Ikagu Shrine|ja|伊香具神社|qid=Q11381016}}. According to shrine traditions, he arrived during ancient times to reclaim undeveloped lands in the area and later protected his descendants.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History and Origins – Ikagu Shrine |url=https://ikagu-jinjya.com/history/ |access-date=2024-04-30 |language=ja}}</ref>

== Genealogy ==

Ikatsuno Mikoto is described as the son of {{ill|Mishokutsuomi no Mikoto|qid=Q135505720}} and the husband of the youngest celestial maiden (*Tennyo*). According to the *{{ill|Ōmi no Kuni Fudoki|ja|近江国風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omi no Kuni Fudoki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11638480}}* excerpts, his children are identified as Omichito (Omichito-no-Mikoto, later known as *臣知人命*<ref>*{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}*, Vol. 11, Sakyo Kamibetsu-jin Section, Nakatomi lineage.</ref>), {{ill|Nashitomi|ja|梨迹臣命|qid=Q108616765}}, Izerihime, and Nazerihime.
